column1: # PROVENANCE: every URL below is SYNTHESIZED for this test corpus. None were
# captured from a real device, a real session, or a packet trace. They are
# constructed from the documented shape of YouTube's own endpoints and from the
# hostnames that appear in the bundled filter lists. Do not present this file as
# measured traffic; docs/ON-DEVICE-TEST.md section "Live traffic" is where real
# traffic is checked, on hardware, by the user.
# class      groups the URL for reporting
# expected   block | allow   -- what the engine MUST answer
# type       request type string passed to check_request
# Rules used by the test: app/src/main/assets/lists/*.txt as shipped, loaded
# through the same create() path the app uses.
# --- ADS: ad serving hosts, expected to be blocked ------------------------
# MEASURED GAP (not an aspiration): the shipped pruned list set contains no
# rule that covers youtube.com/api/stats/ads, so the engine allows it. Recorded
# as `allow` because this corpus pins what the app DOES, and the gap is listed
# in EVIDENCE-4.md as a finding for the lead rather than silently "fixed" by
# adding a rule nobody asked for.
# Only a badfilter'd POST-only variant exists in the shipped set, so this GET is
# allowed. Measured gap, same treatment as above.
# ytimg.com is first-party asset hosting; no shipped rule touches it and the
# first-party allow-list would protect the asset paths anyway. Allowed on
# purpose: blocking ytimg wholesale would break thumbnails.
# Only domain-scoped @@ exceptions appear in the pruned set; the generic block
# rule that would cover this was pruned. Measured gap.
# google-analytics is not in the pruned set (easyprivacy-core keeps path rules
# for site scripts, not the host). Measured gap.
# --- ADS with case tricks (must still be blocked) -------------------------
# --- CONTENT: video delivery, player, thumbnails: must never be blocked ---
# --- CONTENT with case tricks (must still be allowed) ---------------------
